reviewNote: All religious rulings, dua wording and optional/obligatory classifications require review by a qualified scholarly board, with Hanafi-oriented defaults and transparent madhhab notes.
vision: Our aim is not to turn the sacred rites into entertainment. We use gentle stories, age-appropriate rehearsal and reflection so that children understand what Muslims do in Hajj and Umrah, why they do it, and how the lessons can make them truthful, patient, kind and helpful at home.
promise: The child is rewarded inside the app for learning, remembering, solving ethical dilemmas and practising good habits. The app never scores the value of a real Tawaf, prayer, dua or Hajj before Allah, and never certifies ritual validity.
boundaries: Learning is open to all ages. Real Hajj travel is subject to current Saudi and country-of-departure permissions: Pakistan’s 2026 Hajj policy excluded those under 12; reconfirm for every Hajj season. [S04]

A child who performs Hajj may be rewarded, but a prepubescent child’s Hajj does not discharge the obligatory adult Hajj when it later becomes due. Explain this in the parent layer, not as a scary child-facing rule. [S05]
Umrah and Hajj are not interchangeable. Hajj occurs at specified times and has additional rites; Umrah follows Ihram, Tawaf, Sa‘i and Tahallul. [S01][S02]

The Prophet ﷺ is never illustrated or voiced. Prophets, the sacred rites and historical figures are treated respectfully. Historical dialogues are clearly fictional teaching devices, never falsely attributed quotations.

No children are encouraged to approach dangerous crowds, perform actual Rami as a game, approach heights or mountains for completion, break group supervision, or use a phone while moving in dense crowds.
Madinah ziyarat is a separate optional visit, not a requirement for Hajj or Umrah. Historical places are not presented as having special worship rewards without evidence.
All religious rulings, dua wording and optional/obligatory classifications require review by a qualified scholarly board, with Hanafi-oriented defaults and transparent madhhab notes.
missionLoop: Mission loop: Story → Discover → Learn the rule → Try a safe virtual rehearsal → Choose the kind action → Dua echo → Check understanding → Daily action → Muhasabah. In a real travel setting, the parent opens a quiet-reference companion rather than a game.
progressNote: Use an “Explorer’s Notebook” with collected learning pages, not “spiritual coins.” Each mission has three academic completion types: Heard the story; Understood the idea; Practised the value. Make missed questions a chance to learn rather than a punishment. No time pressure and no leaderboard.
devCheck: DEV CHECK: Show three completion states (not started / learning completed / parent-marked real action); do not mark worship as valid. Parent can open lesson source and safety note.

ages.label: Little Explorers
ages.content: 60–90-second narrated episodes; match, point, count, colour, repeat a short phrase with parent. No reading dependence.
ages.session: One idea per screen; unscored practice; 3–5 minutes max with adult.

ages.label: Kindness Travellers
ages.content: 2–4-minute stories; tap sequence; drag-and-drop, Arabic audio, gentle choice tasks, parent dialogue.

ages.label: Young Guides
ages.content: 4–7-minute deeper lessons; sequence logic, evidence, fiqh-labelled notes, scenarios, journal and service missions.

ageNote: Age 3–5 content is also usable as parent-read-aloud. Every mission carries the same central value, but not the same reading load. For 10–14 years, avoid childish jokes, excessive mascot animations or prizes for worship.

scenes.title: The Journey Notebook

dialogue.speaker: Salaam
dialogue.line: We are preparing for a special journey to Makkah.

dialogue.speaker: Imaan
dialogue.line: Are we going there only to see a beautiful place?

dialogue.speaker: Salamah
dialogue.line: We hope to worship Allah and learn better patience and kindness.

dialogue.speaker: Akhlaq
dialogue.line: Then can we prepare our hearts as well as our bags?

dialogue.speaker: Dadi Jaan
dialogue.line: That is a beautiful beginning. Each step should teach us something we can live every day.

scenes.interaction: Child opens two illustrated suitcases: “things to carry” and “good manners to carry.” The second receives patience, gratitude, honesty and helpfulness. The first receives clothing and water with a parent safety note.
scenes.check: “Is Umrah only a sightseeing trip?” Correct: No; it is worship with specific rites. Feedback: “Well done. The purpose guides our actions.”

scenes.title: The Seven Circuits

dialogue.speaker: Imaan
dialogue.line: I see a picture of the Black Stone. Should I push forward to reach it?

dialogue.speaker: Sheikh Uncle
dialogue.line: Never harm another person for a recommended action. Begin each Tawaf circuit at the correct reference point, but you do not have to touch the Stone.

dialogue.speaker: Akhlaq
dialogue.line: What if I forget my practice count?

dialogue.speaker: Salamah
dialogue.line: In this lesson, we can practise again. In real worship, ask a guardian for the correct guidance.

dialogue.speaker: Zameer
dialogue.line: Kindness is not an interruption to worship; it is part of our conduct.

scenes.interaction: A stationary overhead diagram highlights one circuit at a time, without imitating a crowded “speed run.” The child learns clockwise versus counterclockwise by selecting the correct directional arrow; use no movement of religious actors as arcade coins.
scenes.check: “How many full circuits?” Seven. “What if people are crowded?” Protect them and follow safe routes.

scenes.title: Hajar’s Effort

dialogue.speaker: Dadi Jaan
dialogue.line: Long ago, Hajar showed trust in Allah while she took action to care for her child.

dialogue.speaker: Imaan
dialogue.line: So trusting Allah does not mean sitting still?

dialogue.speaker: Dadi Jaan
dialogue.line: Exactly. We ask Allah for help and do what is right and possible.

dialogue.speaker: Akhlaq
dialogue.line: Then I will try again when my homework is difficult—and ask for help when I need it.

dialogue.speaker: Sheikh Uncle
dialogue.line: Safa and Marwah are among the signs of Allah. Our Sa‘i follows the prescribed route.

scenes.interaction: On-screen path shows Safa to Marwah as length 1, then Marwah to Safa as length 2, continuing to seven and ending at Marwah. For preschool children use seven numbered dots. Do not present a full round-trip as one length.
scenes.check: “What is the seventh destination?” Marwah. Action card: “Try your difficult good task again.”

scenes.title: Arafat and the Gentle Tongue

dialogue.speaker: Akhlaq
dialogue.line: Why is the Day of Arafat so important?

dialogue.speaker: Sheikh Uncle
dialogue.line: Standing at Arafat is central to Hajj, and pilgrims spend the day in worship and supplication.

dialogue.speaker: Imaan
dialogue.line: I sometimes argue when I am tired.

dialogue.speaker: Zameer
dialogue.line: Remember: good manners are also for difficult moments.

dialogue.speaker: Dadi Jaan
dialogue.line: The Qur’an teaches pilgrims to avoid disputes. You can practise this lesson at home today.

scenes.interaction: Child chooses a response when another learner cuts ahead in a school queue. The calm, safe option receives educational feedback. No child is led to imitate actual Arafat movement physically.
scenes.check: “Which action follows the lesson of Arafat?” Make dua and treat others well.

scenes.title: The Jamarat are Not Targets

dialogue.speaker: Imaan
dialogue.line: I saw a picture of small pebbles. Are pilgrims throwing at a monster?

dialogue.speaker: Sheikh Uncle
dialogue.line: No. Rami is a prescribed act of Hajj; we do not invent a monster or devil to hit.

dialogue.speaker: Akhlaq
dialogue.line: Then we should not turn it into a throwing game!

dialogue.speaker: Salaam
dialogue.line: Correct. Crowded places require special care and obedience to safety instructions.

dialogue.speaker: Zameer
dialogue.line: Learning to resist a bad choice is a safe challenge we can practise now.

scenes.interaction: Child orders the numbered Jamarat markers on a flat educational diagram. A separate ethics challenge concerns not throwing objects at people. Never animate stones hitting a character.
scenes.check: “What is the safest response near crowded Jamarat?” Follow the official route and responsible adults.

scenes.title: Madinah and Meaningful Love

dialogue.speaker: Akhlaq
dialogue.line: Is Madinah part of the Hajj requirement?

dialogue.speaker: Sheikh Uncle
dialogue.line: It is a blessed visit, but visiting Madinah is not a condition for the validity of Hajj or Umrah.

dialogue.speaker: Imaan
dialogue.line: How do we show love for the Prophet ﷺ?

dialogue.speaker: Dadi Jaan
dialogue.line: By learning and following his guidance, sending salawat and practising good manners.

dialogue.speaker: Salamah
dialogue.line: Let us take those lessons into our home as well.

scenes.interaction: Child sorts “Hajj rite,” “Umrah rite,” and “separate visit.” Correct feedback is never framed as judging who is more devoted.
scenes.check: “Does a family who cannot visit Madinah have an incomplete Hajj?” No. Source label: [S10].

duaIntro: All Arabic is provided as editable text for the publisher. Children learn meaning before memorisation. The app shall not imply these are all obligatory or fixed at every station. Hadith text/grade and Arabic diacritics must be verified by the scholarly editorial board before recording.

duas.title: Talbiyah — during Ihram
duas.arabic: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
duas.meaning: Here I am at Your service, O Allah. You have no partner. Praise, blessings and sovereignty belong to You.
duas.note: Short echo for younger ages; full text for older learners.

duas.title: Qur’anic dua for good
duas.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
duas.meaning: Our Lord, give us good in this life and in the Hereafter and protect us from the Fire.
duas.note: Explain that this is an authentic general dua; useful during Tawaf.

duas.title: Asking for knowledge
duas.meaning: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
duas.note: Best first memory card for ages 3–5.

duas.title: Repentance of Adam and Hawwa
duas.arabic: رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ
duas.meaning: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will be among the losers.
duas.note: For gentle lessons on apologising and changing behaviour.

duas.title: Dua for parents
duas.arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسَابُ
duas.meaning: My Lord, forgive me, my parents and the believers on the Day of Reckoning.
duas.note: Parent-led discussion; not a fixed pilgrimage-only dua.

duas.title: When entering a mosque
duas.meaning: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.
duas.note: Teach general mosque etiquette, not exclusive to Makkah.

duas.title: When leaving a mosque
duas.meaning: O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty.

duas.title: Takbir
duas.source: Rami Takbir in Sahih al-Bukhari 1753; also general dhikr
duas.note: Explain context separately; never use for throwing-game animation.

duas.title: Tahlil — oneness of Allah
duas.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
duas.meaning: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone. His is the dominion and praise, and He has power over all things.
duas.note: Advanced full memorisation, younger learners repeat first phrase.
duas.shortEcho: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ

duas.title: At Safa: Qur’anic opening
duas.arabic: إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ
duas.meaning: Indeed Safa and Marwah are among the signs of Allah.
duas.note: Make clear this is a verse, not a newly invented dua.

duas.title: Simple Tasbih
duas.meaning: Glory and praise be to Allah.
duas.note: General dhikr, not mandatory at a fixed pilgrimage location.

duas.title: Prayer for patience and courage
duas.arabic: رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا
duas.meaning: Our Lord, pour patience upon us and make our feet firm.
duas.note: Good for a school challenge; not a ritual-specific formula.

duas.title: Qur’anic travel remembrance
duas.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ
duas.meaning: Glory to the One Who has subjected this to us; to our Lord we will return.
duas.note: Explain as a portion used in travel remembrance.

duas.title: Salawat — concise learning card
duas.meaning: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad.
duas.source: Short permitted salawat; full transmitted Ibrahimiyyah formula in scholar-approved advanced card (Bukhari 3370)
duas.note: Not presented as a complete replacement for prayer-specific salawat.

parent.hajjDaysNote: DEV NOTE: This is a teaching map, not a universal legal order. Timing, variations, exceptions and school-based details must be route- and scholar-reviewed.
companion: If a family requests travel support, open a parent-only reference experience that explains the proper route, safety, official sources and general guidance. Avoid making child input the authoritative record of Tawaf, Sa‘i or Hajj completion. Parent mode never certifies the validity of rituals.
Child mode cannot book Hajj/Umrah services, purchase travel, request location permission, or mark an adult rite as completed.
The adult route selector must show Tamattu‘/Qiran/Ifrad options where applicable; do not merge divergent Hajj steps.
Do not automatically prescribe handling of missed Miqat, menstruation, delayed Tawaf, Rami on behalf, disability, Ihram violation or Hady: show a qualified-scholar/official-guide referral.
Unverified 2027+ eligibility must never be filled with hard-coded 2026 rules; policy has jurisdiction, season and expiry.
Offline companion may display downloaded verified material; when a permit or transport note expires, clearly show “verify current official instructions.”

faq.q: Does learning Hajj make a child eligible to go?
faq.a: No. The whole curriculum is educational. Actual Hajj participation must follow official age, visa, health and local policy for the relevant season. In Pakistan’s 2026 scheme children below 12 were not eligible; this must not be hard-coded for later years. [S04]

faq.q: Can a young child perform Hajj?
faq.a: The Sunnah recognises the Hajj of a child and a reward for the guardian, but it does not discharge the adult obligation after puberty when its conditions are met. Guardians need current permits and scholarly guidance for actual practice. [S05]

faq.q: Is Umrah compulsory for a young child?
faq.a: Do not pressure a child with adult obligations. Educational practice may be enjoyed at any age, while real Umrah should be supervised and governed by current permissions and fiqh advice.

faq.q: What if a child does not memorise the duas?
faq.a: Memorisation is gradual. The app must allow listening, understanding, repeating and general permitted dua; it should not invent mandatory formulas for every Tawaf round.

faq.q: Can children touch or kiss the Black Stone?
faq.a: No one should push, risk injury or break supervision to reach it. Touching it is not a condition of Tawaf. Child safety comes first.

faq.q: What if a child becomes lost, unwell or overheated?
faq.a: Stop the lesson/game. Follow official safety directions and seek help from a responsible adult or local emergency services; medical safety comes before app completion.

faq.q: What about an older girl who has begun menstruating?
faq.a: Offer an age-appropriate, private and parent-gated explanation. Menstruation affects Tawaf rules; the app must not give an automated personal fatwa or declare ritual validity. Consult a qualified scholar and guardian.

faq.q: What if a ritual was missed or an Ihram restriction was broken?
faq.a: The app records an “I need help” note, explains why this can affect duties, and routes to a knowledgeable adult or qualified scholar. No guessing and no automatic penalty calculator.

faq.q: Does a Madinah visit complete Hajj or Umrah?
faq.a: No. Madinah is a separate blessed visit; the validity of pilgrimage is not dependent on visiting it.

faq.q: May a child use the app during an actual Tawaf or Rami?
faq.a: Do not prompt active games during rituals or moving crowds. A guardian may view downloaded guidance safely when stationary and appropriate.
